cards.text: Psalm 86 is a prayer of David, Israel's king. He opens with no small talk at all: incline Your ear, O LORD, and answer me. And right away, he tells God why.

cards.question: David asks the LORD to lean in and answer him. What reason does David give?

answers.text: He is the king of Israel
He has served God for years

cards.text: Then David keeps going: preserve my soul, save Your servant who trusts in You. He even tells God, "You are my God;" short, clear, no fine print.

cards.question: As David asks the Lord to be merciful, he says he only calls to the Lord once in a while.

cards.text: All day long, friend. Like a phone with the redial button STUCK. Then he prays, "Bring joy to Your servant, for to You, O Lord, I lift up my soul."

cards.question: David is asking the Lord for a LOT. What does David say the Lord is like toward all who call on Him?

cards.text: So David asks again: hear my prayer, O LORD, attend to my plea for mercy. I respect the persistence, friend, because I once begged the Millers' oven to warm up faster and it NEVER listened.

cards.question: David says he calls on the Lord in his day of distress because the Lord ___ him.

cards.text: Now David stops asking for a minute and starts bragging on God: "O Lord, there is none like You among the gods, nor any works like Yours." Nobody. Not close. Not on their BEST day.

cards.question: With none like the Lord, David looks ahead. What does David say all the nations God has made will do?
David says the Lord is one great god among many great gods.

cards.text: Then the prayer turns: David isn't asking for rescue now. He wants to LEARN, like the one coworker who actually reads the training manual.

cards.question: David asks the LORD to teach him His ___ so that he may walk in His truth.

cards.text: Next David asks, "Give me an undivided heart," a heart that's all in, not half and half. Half and half is me with the snooze button: half awake, half asleep, ALL the way late.

cards.question: David asks the LORD for an undivided heart. What does he want it for?

answers.text: So that he may fear God's name
So that he may rule with wisdom
So that he may forget his troubles

cards.text: Then he promises, "I will praise You, O Lord my God, with all my heart; I will glorify Your name forever." He asked for an undivided heart, and now he's praising with ALL of it.

cards.question: David gives a reason for all that praise. What does he say God's great loving devotion has done for him?

answers.text: Delivered him from the depths of Sheol
Made him king over all Israel

cards.text: Then trouble walks in. Arrogant men rise against David, a band of ruthless men seeks his life, and they have no regard for God.

cards.question: Even with ruthless men after him, David says the Lord is slow to anger.

cards.text: So David goes one more round: turn to me, have mercy, grant Your strength to Your servant, save the son of Your maidservant. Same man who started this prayer poor and needy, still knocking on the same door.

cards.question: David asks the LORD for a sign of His goodness so that David's ___ may see it and be ashamed.
David ends the psalm still waiting, saying the LORD has not helped him yet.

findings.problem: The card retells Psalm 86:2 but drops David's reason, "for I am godly." This is one of the reasons David gives God in the opening verses, and no other card covers it, so the baker leaves without it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't hold together. Respecting David's persistence "because" an oven never listened is a non sequitur, and a baker would have to work out how the two connect.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: The joke adds a new moment to Papa Dorin's backstory in the Millers' kitchen: begging the Millers' oven to warm up faster. Jokes may only make up small moments around his bakery. They may not add to the Millers' kitchen story.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The false statement joins two claims: "still waiting" and "the LORD has not helped him yet." In Psalm 86:17 David is still asking for a sign of God's goodness, so a baker could argue that "still waiting" is true. That muddies whether the statement as a whole is false.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
